- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.23) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.11) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend persistence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overforecast; when sentiment is negative, underforecast — adjust forecast by 0.5–1.5% downward for negative sentiment, upward for positive.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend if sentiment flips — model often ignores sentiment reversal and continues trend.
